audit.whatIsWrong: This side's chart read Neeko / Skill / Yone / Yone / Neeko / Yone / Yone. The already-audited mirror (neeko__yone) sets row 0 to Skill, rows 1-5 to Neeko and row 6 to Yone. The two pages disagreed on five of seven rows, including 'who wins Level 2'.
audit.why: Neeko's lane tools stay online continuously — Tangle-Barbs at 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s and Blooming Burst at 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s — so the gaps Yone needs do not appear on their own before items; Yone's edge is the 2-item side lane, which is the row he keeps.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-5 aligned to the mirror as one atomic paired group, with ratings and every contradicting whys / phases[].why line rewritten so the prose stops claiming Yone owns levels 2-5.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 text said Pop Blossom 'needs a windup' and is 'telegraphed and dodgeable', with no mention that the preparation is hidden while she is disguised — which is the entire point of the ability.
audit.why: Riot's text states outright that the preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised, so the tell a player is told to watch for does not exist when it matters.
audit.corrected: Pop Blossom restated: the windup is hidden under a disguise, the tell is the clone, and it is a 90-120s cooldown to punish once spent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two content fields told the player Neeko's roots were 'Windwall-able' and that he could 'dodge, Windwall, or interrupt' her ult. Yone has no Wind Wall — that is Yasuo. Fate Sealed was also described as setting up knockups; it blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls, and the knockup is Mortal Steel's second-stack cast.
audit.why: Riot ability text in the brief; the mirror recorded the identical Fate Sealed correction, so both directions now read the same.
audit.corrected: Windwall references removed and replaced with sidestepping a 1000-range root; Fate Sealed restated as blink-behind-and-pull in phases[4].why and breakdown.late.

edits.before: Level 2 tilts to you as your dash lets you close on a Neeko with no escape once her E is spent.
edits.after: Level 2 is hers — Tangle-Barbs roots on a 12s cooldown and her Q bounces refill the poke.

edits.before: Level 3 evens out again while her E root and Q burst are back up to punish your approach.
edits.after: Level 3 is hers too — E root into Blooming Burst punishes every approach you make.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 favour you — your window-punish aggression beats her once her cooldowns are down.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay hers: Tangle-Barbs drops to 10.5s and Q to 7.5s, so gaps are rare.

edits.before: At 6 it's a skill check: her Pop Blossom threatens a burst kill but is telegraphed and dodgeable.
edits.after: At 6 she leads: Pop Blossom's windup is hidden while she is disguised, so the stun lands.

edits.before: First item is yours as your DPS dives her squishy body the moment she blows her root.
edits.after: First item still hers — one landed root sets a full combo before your DPS lands.

edits.before: W shield-grit covers every exchange you start. Only take the trade when Neeko's Tangle-Barbs is down.
edits.after: Tangle-Barbs roots on 12s and grows through a champion. Take the trade only in the window after she spends it.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Neeko must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online, but hers punishes harder: E root into Blooming Burst. Hold the wave near you so she must step into Q3 range.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Tangle-Barbs's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Tangle-Barbs falls to 10.5s here, so the safe gaps shrink. Trade only on a whiffed root; if behind, farm safe and wait for items.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Neeko's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks behind her and pulls — it is not a knockup. Pop Blossom's windup is hidden while she wears a disguise.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Tangle-Barbs's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King helps, but a landed Tangle-Barbs still sets her full combo — force only on a whiffed root.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge — build your teamfight around that. Neeko carry threat: 7/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks behind their back line and pulls it to you — build your teamfight around that. Neeko carry threat: 7/10 — shift to picks and wave control if she gets ahead.

edits.before: Her Pop Blossom (R) needs a windup and a stun to land cleanly; you can E out of it or Fate Sealed her mid-cast, and your all-in threat post-6 outweighs her single burst combo.
edits.after: Pop Blossom (R) has a windup, but it is hidden while she is disguised as an ally — the tell is the clone, not the cast. On a 90-120s cooldown, punish hard the moment she spends it.

edits.before: You stay favoured — she's a squishy mage you can hard-engage with E and delete, and her only defence is Windwall-able roots and a telegraphed ult; catch her without R and she folds.
edits.after: You stay favoured — a squishy mage you hard-engage with Soul Unbound and delete. Her defence is a 1000-range root you sidestep and a 90-120s ult; catch her without R and she folds.

edits.before: You stay favoured into items — Neeko is a squishy burst mage you hard-engage with E and cleave down. Her survival hinges on landing a root or a hidden ult, both of which you can dodge, Windwall, or interrupt with Fate Sealed.
edits.after: You stay favoured into items — Neeko is a squishy burst mage you hard-engage with Soul Unbound and cleave down. Her survival hinges on a 1000-range root or a disguised Pop Blossom; you have no windwall, so sidestep or pull her with Fate Sealed.

notes: Same Windwall error as the Nautilus page: two fields told a Yone player to Windwall Neeko's root. Yone has no Wind Wall. suspectNames flagged 'Her Pop Blossom' in spikes[1] — that is a false positive, Pop Blossom is the correct name; the real problem in that field was the claim that the ult is telegraphed, when Riot's text says the preparation is hidden under a disguise. Chart aligned to the already-audited mirror.
